summary: Preston County, WV line tower planned 1925 for joint Maryland and West Virginia use; the register says it was destroyed by fire in the 1980s; the site is now inside Alpine Lake Resort.

facts.status_note: Register says destroyed by fire in the 1980s; the land is now part of Alpine Lake Resort

access.note: Alpine Lake Resort is open to the public, but the neighborhood where the tower stood is for residents only

events.note: Construction announced in January 1925 as a 60-foot steel tower replacing a wooden lookout; in operation by July 1925
Owned jointly by Maryland and West Virginia, per a 1926 Charleston Gazette item reprinted on Forest Lookouts
Register says destroyed by a fire in the 1980s and gives the 1980s as its removal date. 1980 is a placeholder for the decade; no exact year is in our sources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1926 Charleston Gazette item says the two states owned it jointly; the register says Maryland owned and maintained it. The story reports both

notes_for_editor: Source conflict on ownership (1926 joint vs register's Maryland). The register gives the 1980s both as the fire year and as the removal date; the Forest Lookouts page gives no end date. The 1980 event year is a placeholder for the decade. A Maryland DNR fire tower poster appeared only in a search snippet (the fetch returned 404), claiming a wooden 1940s tower; that conflicts with the 1925 steel-tower reports, so it is not used. The FFLA Maryland list has a separate Snaggy Mountain (Pitch Pine Rock) entry in Garrett County with unknown coordinates, marked gone; check whether it is this tower before merging. The 60-foot height is the 1925 announced height. The register photos are already in the record.
